Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Combat Recorder
Description: Writes one compressed JSON-lines file per duty: every action you, your party and enemies use (with damage/heal numbers), buffs and debuffs gained and lost, HP/MP and positions twice a second, casts, deaths and target changes. Party members are recorded by job and slot, never by name. /crec mark <note> drops a marker you can point to later ("downtime here"). Nothing leaves your PC. Also a DPS meter in game: party DPS, rDPS and aDPS (raid buffs credited to whoever gave them), HPS, damage taken, crit and direct hit rates, deaths and per-skill breakdowns, counted the way ACT does (encounter DPS, DoTs and pets included), with the last 10 fights kept.
Punchline: Records your fights (actions, damage, heals, buffs, HP, movement) to compact local files for review.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Cooldown Grid
Description: Pick any of your job's cooldown abilities and sort them into groups. Each group gets its own window: a grid of ability icons showing time remaining and charges. Click an icon to use the ability, just like a hotbar button. Settings are saved per job; All four tanks ship with a starter layout. Also a small floating "Plugins" button that stays up during cutscenes: plugin installer, updates, Dalamud settings, or any plugin's window, without typing a command.
Punchline: Clickable cooldown grids, grouped into Defensive (self), Defensive (group), Support, and your own groups.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Map Click Nav
Description: Hold a modifier (Ctrl by default) and left-click a spot on any zone's map. Map Click Nav places your flag there, teleports to the nearest attuned aetheryte if that's faster (always, for another zone), mounts with Mount Roulette, and has vnavmesh fly you there if flight is unlocked (or ride there if not). A Stop button appears while traveling. Requires vnavmesh.
Punchline: Ctrl+click any map to teleport, mount, and fly there with vnavmesh.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Materia Manager
Description: Shows your materia by type and grade in your bags, saddlebag and materia retainer. Storage: opening the saddlebag stores bag materia; "pull all" brings it back for transmuting; your materia retainer is topped up to a minimum/maximum of each materia (e.g. 800) when you open it, splitting stacks for exact amounts, and the rest stays in your bags. Transmutation: pick fodder and keep-at-least numbers; it plans batches of five and takes you to Mutamix Bubblypots. English client.
Punchline: Materia in one place: auto-store to saddlebag or retainer, and plan transmutation batches with keep-at-least rules.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Material Stash
Description: Sorts common crafting materials onto your retainers in the order you choose. Gathered materials (mining, botany, fishing) and white, tradeable mob drops used in recipes qualify; boss drops, crafted items and collectables don't, and you can include or exclude anything by hand. Each category (ore, lumber, hides...) gets an ordered list of home retainers, with an overflow order behind it, and items already on a retainer are kept together. Crystals fill retainers in the game's list order, keeping a set amount of each on you. Nothing runs by itself: press "Stash" above the retainer list (after AutoRetainer is done) and it visits each retainer, deposits, and moves on. Stock list: keep a minimum and target of items, or of whole recipes (materials worked out from the recipe); when AutoRetainer sends a retainer out, it is sent for the most-needed item it can bring back. Tidy sorts items between retainers by groups (housing, gear, materials...), name rules and item pins. Keep on me protects what you carry. When nothing on the stock list fits a retainer, it can go for what sells best on your home world instead (with a demand check); those items stay in your bags and can be listed automatically. A Clean-up tab goes through everything on your retainers and suggests what to sell, vendor, turn in, desynthesize, learn, keep for its look or discard (judged by value, the glamour dresser and Armoire, and how easy it is to get again), then carries out what you approve, including a trip to an inn (Lifestream) to put looks in the Armoire or glamour dresser. Indoor furnishings can be taken off your retainers and stored in your house's storeroom (Lifestream takes you home). Scrip goals: keep a number of a scrip-exchange item; it crafts the best-paying collectable (Vulcan or Artisan, materials from bags, retainers, the market board or gathering; gatherer-scrip items are gathered with GatherBuddy Reborn auto-gather), has Turn-In Manager turn it in, and buys the item. ICE break: while Ices Cosmic Exploration (ICE) runs, once retainers are back it lets ICE finish its mission, goes to a bell for AutoRetainer and the stash, returns with Lifestream and starts ICE again. A small window counts ready ventures. Buttons on the saddlebag move mats in or out. English client.
Punchline: One button at the summoning bell puts your gathered and mob-dropped crafting mats and crystals on the right retainers.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Mit Planner
Description: Detects your duty, runs the fight's timeline (cactbot format, synced to the boss's actual abilities), and shows the next mechanics with countdowns and type (tank buster, raid-wide, ...). Attach your cooldowns to specific mechanics per job (tanks and healers get an automatic Default plan; keep several plans per fight), and get a callout a few seconds before each one. Optional per-cooldown auto-use. Ships with every fight cactbot has a timeline for (300+ dungeons, trials, raids and ultimates, refreshed weekly), with tank busters and raid-wides pre-tagged.
Punchline: Boss timeline with countdowns, plus a per-job cooldown plan that tells you what to press and when.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Plugin Hub
Description: Put the plugins you use on bars of icons, laid out in rows and columns like your hotbars, instead of hunting through the plugin list or remembering commands. Click a tile to open that plugin's window, right-click for its settings, or give a tile its own command. Shift+click turns a plugin on or off. Tiles use the plugin's own icon when it has one, and its name when it doesn't; hover for what it does. Make as many bars as you like, each with its own columns, tile size, position and lock, and drag tiles to rearrange them. /hub opens the settings.
Punchline: Hotbar-style bars of plugin buttons: click to open a plugin, right-click for its settings.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Poetics Spender
Description: Pick a topsoil (Thanalan or Shroud). One click teleports you to Idyllshire, buys Unidentifiable Ore/Shell from Hismena with all your Poetics (150 each), and trades it to Bertana for Grade 3 topsoil. A movable alert pops up when your Poetics reach a threshold (1800 by default); click it to run. Requires vnavmesh. English client.
Punchline: Turn your Poetics into Grade 3 topsoil with one click, plus a near-cap alert.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Raise Callouts
Description: Watches your own raise spells (Raise, Resurrection, Ascend, Egeiro, Verraise, Angel Whisper) and posts a callout when you start casting one, or when an instant (Swiftcast/Dualcast) raise lands. Works with rotation plugins because it watches the cast itself, not a hotbar button. One message per raise, skips targets already being raised, editable message, party chat or echo only.
Punchline: Says "Raising <name>" in party chat whenever you raise someone, however it was cast (RotationSolver, macros, hotbar).

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Rescue Helper
Description: Asks BossMod (Reborn) which spots are dangerous right now and checks each party member's position. Anyone standing in a danger zone that resolves within a few seconds turns red with a countdown. Click their row to Rescue them, or switch to automatic. It only Rescues when your own spot is safe, Rescue is ready and in range, and never pulls a tank holding enemies or a player carrying a mechanic marker (spread/stack). Needs BossMod or BossMod Reborn.
Punchline: Healers: a party panel that shows who's standing in an AoE about to go off. Click to Rescue them, or let it Rescue automatically.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Retainer Gear
Description: Records each retainer's equipped gear when you open them, then works out the highest item level available for their job and level from crafted gear, dungeon drops and uncapped-tomestone gear (no raid or savage gear). Shows what each retainer still needs, a combined shopping list with market board prices (Universalis) for crafted pieces, and marks gear you already own and which retainer it's for. Re-check after you equip upgrades and the list updates.
Punchline: Tracks your retainers' gear and lists the best non-raid upgrades: crafted, dungeon drops, or uncapped tomestones.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Saucer Run
Description: A floating button shows whether today's Mini Cactpot and this week's Jumbo Cactpot are done. Click it and it learns any Triple Triad cards in your bags you don't have yet, teleports to the Gold Saucer, collects Jumbo Cactpot winnings and buys this week's tickets, plays the three Mini Cactpot tickets, then sells your spare cards to the Triple Triad Trader for MGP. The Cactpot games themselves (number picks, the scratch board) are left to Saucy, which must be installed with its Mini Cactpot and Jumbo Cactpot modules on. Walking uses vnavmesh. When the Cactpots are done, the button just does cards. English client.
Punchline: One button for your Gold Saucer chores: Mini Cactpot, Jumbo Cactpot, and Triple Triad cards.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Settings Sync
Description: Backs up the pluginConfigs folder (every plugin, minus an exclude list) to a private GitHub repository and pulls it on your other PCs. Syncs automatically when the game opens and closes, or with a Sync now button. Asks when both PCs changed the same file. History tab keeps the last 5 snapshots, restorable whole or one plugin at a time. Sign in once per PC with your GitHub account (device code); no token to copy around. You create the repository and a small GitHub App yourself; see the README.
Punchline: Keeps your plugin settings the same on every PC, through a private GitHub repo you own.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Tank Stance Manager
Description: MT mode keeps tank stance on at all times. OT mode toggles tank stance to hold your enmity inside a configurable band of the main tank's enmity (default 75%-90%), and turns it on if you are pushed to #3. Supports PLD, WAR, DRK, GNB.
Punchline: Keeps tank stance on as MT, or holds an enmity band as OT.

Author: NoFocusLab
Name: Turn-In Manager
Description: Turns in gear for Grand Company seals with guardrails: never items in a gearset, a maximum item level, rarity (green/blue) and HQ/NQ filters, optional armoury chest. Retrieves materia from qualifying gear first (gear turned in with materia loses it). Before seals would cap, it buys items you choose up to a stock target (e.g. Ventures up to 65,000), then keeps delivering. Preview shows exactly what would be turned in. Scrips: turns in collectables at the Collectable Appraiser and buys an item at the Scrip Exchange, buying before scrips would cap (used by Material Stash scrip goals). Uses vnavmesh to walk, and Lifestream (if installed) to travel to your Grand Company. English client.
Punchline: Grand Company expert delivery with guardrails, materia retrieval first, and seal spending by stock targets.
